source.title: Towards Understanding Multimodal Fine-Tuning: A Case Study into Spatial Features
source.authors: Lachin Naghashyar; Hunar Batra; Ashkan Khakzar; P. Torr; Ronald Clark; Christian Schroeder de Witt; Constantin Venhoff

record.file_problem: No apparent file problem; the full paper and appendix are present.
record.tranche_reason: The paper measures how SAE feature-direction alignment varies by token regime and layer, providing a conditional result relevant to V6. It does not test scale-related convergence between independently trained models.
record.gate_note: The decoder-cosine results bear on V6's claim that measured alignment depends on inputs and settings. The paper does not test convergence with scale, cross-modal alignment between separate vision and language models, or pairwise distances between representations of the same inputs. Other reported results, including spatial-feature ablations and attribution patching, concern spatial reasoning rather than the listed convergence versions.
record.test_reason: The study does not compare independently trained models, seeds, modalities' separate models, or similarity metrics. It warm-starts LLaMA-Scope SAEs and fine-tunes them on LLaVA-More activations of the same Llama-3.1-8B backbone. It then measures, by feature index, how far each decoder direction drifts from its own initialization. That is fine-tuning drift used as a diffing tool, not a measurement of representational convergence. Its dependence on token regime and layer reflects input-distribution mismatch, not a sensitivity of a convergence measure. Li et al. 2015 (an original source) is cited only in related work.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors conclude that multimodal adaptation is structured and localizable. Vision-preferring features rotate during fine-tuning, a subset encodes spatial relations (ablations cut VSR accuracy 9–16 points), and a few mid-layer attention heads drive them. The analysis is limited to one model.
record.recipe_differences: Measures cosine similarity between SAE decoder directions across base and multimodally adapted stages, rather than comparing distances induced by independently trained models on the same inputs; no scale sweep.
record.method_sensitivity: Decoder-cosine alignment varies with token regime and layer depth: image-only and full-sequence dictionaries rotate in shallow layers and align in later layers, while text-only dictionaries remain highly aligned.

fits_no_version.finding: Text-only SAE decoders stay highly aligned to the base LLM dictionary across layers. SAEs warm-started from it and trained on image or full-sequence tokens rotate strongly in shallow layers and realign in deeper layers. Values are given in Fig. 5 only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Multimodal fine-tuning largely preserves a language backbone's SAE feature directions on text tokens, while image-token features diverge in early layers and converge to the language basis in later layers.

record.problems: The claim-relevant cosine results are qualitative in the text, with exact values presented only in figures. The study analyzes a single LLaVA-More model and does not test scale or independently trained model pairs.
record.rows_left_out: Spatial-feature ablation, attribution-patching, feature-selection, reconstruction-error, and OCR results were left out because they do not measure the representation-convergence behavior named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: No scale or capability sweep; no independently trained models compared.
No alignment of separate vision and language models on paired data.
No matched comparison of features across seeds; the random-init SAE is compared by index only.
No mapping, stitching or relative-representation transfer between models is evaluated.
No test of features recurring across different models.
No comparison of similarity measures, their settings, or input sets for a cross-model convergence measure.
No measure of cross-model alignment level, plateau, or its causes.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V6 link treats SAE decoder drift under warm-started fine-tuning as evidence that convergence measures are metric- or data-dependent. The study does not measure convergence between models at all. The cosine compares the same feature index before and after adapting the dictionary, within one backbone. The paper also assumes that SAEs largely transfer between base and fine-tuned models (citing Kissane et al.) to justify the warm-start. It does not test that assumption against any V4 criterion.

versions.untested_parts: Scale, capability, and alignment between independently trained models with different architectures, objectives, or data.
Alignment between separate vision and language models on paired images and captions, and its relationship to their performance.
Feature or subspace convergence across networks of the same architecture trained from different initializations.
Mapping representations between models, stitching, relative representations, or alignment without paired data.
Recurrence of interpretable features or circuits across different models.

The study compares decoder cosine alignment across token regimes and layers, but does not compare alternative similarity measures, test out-of-distribution inputs, or measure pairwise distances between model representations.
Whether alignment plateaus or remains incomplete across independently trained models, and whether shared data or objectives explain convergence.

rows.subject: LLaVA-More (LLaMA 3.1 8B backbone), text-only SAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE decoder directions with the base LLM dictionary using cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between base LLM SAE and VLM-adapted SAE decoder directions
rows.value: Text-only SAEs remain highly aligned across layers.
rows.note: The paper describes the trend in text; exact cosine values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Measures cosine between a warm-started SAE and its own initialization after training on text-token activations of the fine-tuned backbone. This is fine-tuning drift, not convergence between models or metric dependence of a convergence measure.

rows.subject: LLaVA-More (LLaMA 3.1 8B backbone), image-only SAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE decoder directions with the base LLM dictionary using cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between base LLM SAE and VLM-adapted SAE decoder directions
rows.value: Image-only SAEs undergo large rotations in shallow layers.
rows.note: The paper reports the qualitative trend; exact cosine values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Same drift measure on image tokens; the shallow-layer rotation reflects the projector/LLM distribution gap, not a V6 metric or setting dependence. State 'partial' has no meaning relative to any version.

rows.subject: LLaVA-More (LLaMA 3.1 8B backbone), image-only SAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE decoder directions with the base LLM dictionary using cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between base LLM SAE and VLM-adapted SAE decoder directions
rows.value: Image-only SAEs align with the base dictionary in later layers.
rows.note: The paper reports the qualitative trend; exact cosine values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Same drift measure, image-only regime in deeper layers; not a convergence measurement.

rows.subject: LLaVA-More (LLaMA 3.1 8B backbone), full-sequence SAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE decoder directions with the base LLM dictionary using cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between base LLM SAE and VLM-adapted SAE decoder directions
rows.value: Full-sequence SAEs undergo large rotations in shallow layers.
rows.note: The paper reports the qualitative trend; exact cosine values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Same drift measure, full-sequence regime in shallow layers; not a convergence measurement.

rows.subject: LLaVA-More (LLaMA 3.1 8B backbone), full-sequence SAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE decoder directions with the base LLM dictionary using cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between base LLM SAE and VLM-adapted SAE decoder directions
rows.value: Full-sequence SAEs align with the base dictionary in later layers.
rows.note: The paper reports the qualitative trend; exact cosine values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: Same drift measure, full-sequence regime in deeper layers; not a convergence measurement.

rows.subject: Randomly initialized SAE
rows.operation_detail: Compared SAE decoder directions with the base LLM dictionary using cosine similarity.
rows.measure: Cosine similarity between base LLM SAE and randomly initialized SAE decoder directions
rows.value: Randomly initialized SAEs stay largely uncorrelated.
rows.note: The appendix states the qualitative result; exact cosine values are shown only in the figure.
rows.check: The random-init SAE is compared to LLaMA-Scope by feature index with no matching, so near-zero cosine is expected by construction. It cannot bear on V3 seed convergence or V5 universality. It is a control for the warm-start, not a result.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.
